source.title: Model Collapse Is Not a Bug but a Feature in Machine Unlearning for LLMs
source.authors: Yan Scholten; Sophie Xhonneux; Leo Schwinn; Stephan Günnemann

record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own sampling and prefilling attack results on unlearned models. These qualify when prior methods leak and describe PMC as more robust, refining the claim rather than simply using it.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the sampling and prefilling attacks in Figures 4 and 24, and the least-likely-option multiple-choice attack in Figure 5(b). Values are presented graphically without extractable numbers in the supplied text. Other claims about methods cited from prior work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own sampling (100 samples) and prefilling ('The answer is:') leakage attacks on Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct unlearned with IDK, DPO, NPO, SimNPO and its new method PMC. Prefilling recovers substantial forget-set information from IDK, and DPO leaks under sampling. PMC is presented as resisting both attacks. These results bear on A, E and F. B, C and D are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that PMC removes information from model outputs more effectively than target-dependent methods while preserving utility, and that it is more robust to sampling and prefilling attacks. They add that prior methods show side effects (distorted token probabilities, multiple-choice leakage). They state that robustness to relearning or adversarial attacks remains future work and that there are no formal unlearning guarantees.
record.recipe_differences: PMC iteratively fine-tunes on self-generated responses selected for divergence, rather than applying the claim’s recovery attacks or the target-dependent unlearning recipes it compares against.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack type (sampling versus prefilling plus sampling) and unlearning method affect leakage. The paper also reports that unlearning outcomes vary with hyperparameters and gradient checkpointing, but those are not attack-recovery rows here.

fits_no_version.finding: NPO leaves the correct answer as the least-likely multiple-choice option, so picking the least likely option reveals it, even with rephrased answers. PMC shows no such pattern.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Target-dependent unlearning can leak forgotten answers through abnormally suppressed option probabilities (a least-likely-option attack).

fits_no_version.finding: NPO reduces the probability of forget-set tokens in unrelated wikitext contexts (mean difference -0.12, many tokens dropping to zero probability). PMC differences are zero-mean.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Target-based unlearning distorts token probabilities outside the forget context.

record.problems: Attack outcomes are shown in figures without extractable numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The main attack comparison uses Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct; the multiple-choice attack uses a subset of 84 questions. The authors acknowledge that broad robustness to relearning or adversarial attacks is not evaluated.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row cap.

untested.parts: Near-chance targeted accuracy is not measured: leakage is lexical ROUGE-L on TOFU, not benchmark accuracy such as WMDP. No relearning, internal-edit, quantization, rephrasing, jailbreak, language or in-context attacks.
Entirely untested; the authors say robustness to relearning remains future work.
Entirely untested; no activation ablation or probing.
Only prefilling is tested. There is no rephrasing attack (paraphrased-forget is pooled into unlearn quality), no jailbreaks, no other languages, and no in-context information.

PMC is tested only against sampling and prefilling on one model (Llama-3.2-3B). Fine-tuning relearning, activation edits, quantization, rephrasing, jailbreaks, languages and in-context attacks are untested.

missing.what: General-ability retention after PMC: ARC-Challenge, ARC-Easy and MMLU for base vs PMC (e.g. Llama MMLU 0.6041 vs 0.5924), bearing on A's 'keeps general ability' part.

Unlearn quality vs utility Pareto curves for all methods on Phi-1.5, Llama-3.2-3B and Gemma-3-12b. This is greedy ROUGE-L on forget plus paraphrased-forget, the baseline unlearning success relevant to A.

record.verdict_notes: All attack values are figure-only. Row states use the convention 'leakage/recovery effect present or absent'. The sampling attack is decoding-based, so it is linked only to A, not E. The attack experiments are single-seed and use one model (Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct). Leakage is measured by lexical ROUGE-L, so the authors acknowledge semantic leakage could be missed. PMC is the authors' own method, and they note gradient checkpointing changes unlearning trajectories.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports unlearning quality and utility, but does not test targeted-knowledge accuracy against a stated near-chance level. It tests sampling and prefilling attacks, not every simple attack.
No post-unlearning relearning attack using unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten examples.
No activation-direction ablation or test of whether a method blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Tests prefilling followed by sampling, and a multiple-choice least-likely-option attack. Does not test rephrasing prompts alone, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
Tests PMC against sampling and prefilling attacks. Does not test resistance to fine-tuning, activation edits, quantization, rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
